subject: AI use boundaries, operational evidence, and procurement questions - Keystone Health
messages:
From: Avery Bennett <avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@keystonehealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keystone DPA - clarification on ML training / outputs

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Before our commercial team moves forward we need two clarifications: (1) Keystone requires that any customer-provided content is not used to improve vendor models (no-training or no-adaptive training commitment), and (2) we need confirmation on output ownership (we need to ensure generated responses and any derivative output are scoped to Keystone).

Can Redwood confirm operational evidence you can provide to demonstrate the no-training commitment (audit logs, subprocessor attestations, routing/residency guarantees)? Also, our legal team has asked about cross-border subprocessors and whether Redwood has any planned vendor transfers in the next 12 months.

If possible, could you point us to the ops artifacts and an estimated timeline to produce them? Procurement would like to get this completed before EOD Friday.

Appreciate the help —
Avery

--
Avery Bennett
Head of Procurement, Keystone Health
avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Bennett <avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Keystone DPA - clarification on ML training / outputs

Thanks Avery — quick note to acknowledge and loop in David and Laura from privacy/ops. We'll put together an evidence pack and confirm subprocessors. High level answers below; David will follow up with specifics and the checklist.

- No-training: Redwood can commit to a customer-specific non-improvement mode for enterprise customers via a contractual no-adaptive-training clause and operational routing that prevents tenant data from entering any training pipelines.
- Evidence: we can produce a combination of (a) subprocessor attestation list with data flow diagrams, (b) audit log extracts showing request routing and KMS residency, and (c) a signed ops checklist that maps to the DPA redlines.
- Subprocessors: current list attached; planned transfers in the next 12 months are limited to routine cloud provider expansions (we commit to notify 30 days in advance).

I'll ask David to send the formal evidence items and an estimated delivery timeline.

Next steps: David — can you confirm the checklist items and whether we can produce the first bundle by Thursday EOD? Laura — can you assist with the redlines doc if legal needs versioned responses?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: david_kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Bennett <avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone DPA - clarification on ML training / outputs

Hi Avery — David from Privacy/Compliance here. Appreciate the clear asks; below are concrete artifacts we can provide and the current ETA. Im attaching a short ops-evidence checklist that maps to your procurement asks.

Artifacts we can provide now (Tier 1):
- Subprocessor inventory (current list + SOC2 status)
- Operational routing diagram (how enterprise tenant traffic is isolated)
- Audit log extract template showing request routing and KMS key usage (redacted PII)
- Signed attestation from our Subprocessor Manager confirming no-training configuration for your tenant

Planned artifacts (Tier 2) — delivery by Thu 2026-05-21 EOD:
- Export of sample audit slices (time-bound, redacted) for your compliance review
- A short runbook describing how we enforce the non-improvement mode (routing, KV cache policies, model variant fallback)
- Confirmation of data residency commitments for any planned cloud region expansions (we will not move Keystone data without written notice)

On subprocessors/transfers: there are no planned changes that would move production data to a new third-party subprocessor other than standard cloud region availability in the next 12 months. Any onboarding of new inference partners would be subject to our subprocessor gating and written notice.

If you need signed language in the DPA that references specific ops artifacts, we can propose exhibit language that ties the contractual commitment to the evidence bundle.

Let me know if procurement accepts the Tiered evidence approach and I'll queue the artifacts for delivery.

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwoodinference.com

From: Avery Bennett <avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@keystonehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone DPA - clarification on ML training / outputs

David / Marissa — thanks, that plan works. Procurement accepts the Tier 1 bundle today and well review Tier 2 Thursday EOD. Two small asks before legal executes: (1) can Redwood include the phrase "no adaptive training or model improvement" in the DPA section 3.2 and reference the attached ops-evidence checklist as Exhibit B; (2) wed like a single-page attestation signed by your Head of Privacy confirming the configuration is in place for Keystone (we can accept a PII-redacted audit slice as part of Tier 1).

If you can send the Exhibit B draft and a signed attestation by end of day Thursday, procurement will route the DPA to legal for final signature.

Best,
Avery

--
Avery Bennett
Head of Procurement, Keystone Health
avery.bennett@keystonehealth.com
